newsitem.title: UK: IBCA may raise Creditanstalt ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA may raise Creditanstalt ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had put Creditanstalt Bankverein's short and long-term ratings of A1 and A plus on RatingWatch with positive implications.
At the same time, IBCA affirmed the short and long-term ratings of Bank Austria of A1 plus and AA respectively.

"This follows the Austrian government's announcement that it had accepted Bank Austria's 17.2 billion Austrian schilling offer for its effective 70 percent stake in Creditanstalt, subject to approval by the European Union," IBCA said in a statement.
"The takeover will create a dominant domestic banking group and within Europe a regional banking group of significant size."

IBCA said that a pre-condition of the agreement was that AVZ, the city of Vienna foundation, agreed to reduce its current 45 percent stake in Bank Austria to below 20 percent over a period of seven years.
But it added: "IBCA understands that the city of Vienna will continue to guarantee the liabilities of Bank Austria through AVZ."

It said the government had committed itself to an amendment to the Savings Banks Act, giving the option to savings banks owned by municipalities to either pay a guarantee fee to their municipality or accept the waiver of the guarantee.
"IBCA will review Bank Austria's ratings in the light of action taken under the new law," the statement said.
IBCA said Creditanstalt would remain an independent entity for a period of at least five years and would not directly benefit from the deficiency guarantee of the city of Vienna.
"The potential for substantial synergies will be delayed as a result of the deferral of a full merger of the two entities," it said.
